slides.heading: Airport Connections
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Airport Connections, a very hard graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Minimum number of new one-way routes from the starting airport so every airport is reachable.
Collapse strongly connected components (Tarjan) and count SCCs with in-degree 0, excluding the one containing the start.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Minimum number of new one-way routes from the starting airport so every airport is reachable. Collapse strongly connected components (Tarjan) and count SCCs with in-degree 0, excluding the one containing the start.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Only unreachable airports matter; pick those that unlock the most others first.
slides.narration: Only unreachable airports matter; pick those that unlock the most others first.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each, count airports reachable only through it
slides.narration: Step by step. First, find unreachable airports. Second, for each, count airports reachable only through it. Third, sort by that count. Fourth, greedily connect.
